10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates extracting simple temporal features, already covered in this topic, from a sequence of frame values.

code.content:
import random
random.seed(0)

def simulate_frame_features(num_frames, feature_dim=3):
    # already covered as video as a sequence of frames in this topic
    return [[round(random.uniform(0, 1), 2) for _ in range(feature_dim)] for _ in range(num_frames)]

frames = simulate_frame_features(num_frames=5)
print(f"Per-frame spatial features (already covered as spatial features in this topic):")
for i, frame in enumerate(frames):
    print(f"  frame {i}: {frame}")

def temporal_difference(frames):
    # already covered as temporal features in this topic
    diffs = []
    for i in range(1, len(frames)):
        diff = [round(frames[i][d] - frames[i-1][d], 2) for d in range(len(frames[i]))]
        diffs.append(diff)
    return diffs

diffs = temporal_difference(frames)
print(f"\nFrame-to-frame differences (already covered as temporal features in this topic):")
for i, diff in enumerate(diffs):
    print(f"  frame {i} -> frame {i+1}: {diff}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows how frame-to-frame differences genuinely capture motion information that a single, isolated frame alone genuinely cannot represent, exactly the temporal feature idea already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Video models extend image understanding across the added dimension of time.
A video can be treated as an ordered sequence of individual frame images.
Spatial features describe content within one frame; temporal features describe change across frames.
Three dimensional convolutions slide a kernel across space and time together, capturing motion directly.
Recurrent approaches feed frame features into an RNN, accumulating information across the sequence.
Modern transformer based video models treat frames or spacetime patches as tokens in a sequence.
Processing many frames instead of one multiplies compute and memory cost significantly.
Video models suit tasks needing motion and change; plain image models suffice for static content.
